intent: Stop the WireGuard/SSH firewall from silently cutting every Docker container off the internet, and rebuild Docker's own nft rules after the ruleset flush that deletes them.
scope: Non-goal: no change to the input chain, the WireGuard port, sshd hardening or the LAN/DNS rules
Non-goal: no change to Docker's own iptables management (DOCKER-USER stays untouched)
changes: forward chain keeps policy drop but now accepts established/related plus traffic in or out of docker0 and any br-* bridge, so it stops vetoing Docker's own chains at the same netfilter hook
new restore_docker_rules() restarts dockerd after a successful apply, because 'flush ruleset' deletes Docker's tables and dockerd only rebuilds them on its next network event

verification.command: vm new nftfw && vm run nftfw 'bash /tmp/nft_docker_guest_test.sh'
verification.evidence: Arch guest, docker installed, alpine wget probe to 1.1.1.1: BASELINE=reachable -> OLD(unpatched ruleset)=blocked -> NEW(patched ruleset)=reachable; sshd active throughout. The OLD leg reproduces the outage this fixes.
NFT SYNTAX OK for the file write_nftables_ruleset() generates with ALLOW_WEB/ALLOW_DNS both true.

verification.command: live host check after applying the same five rules by hand
verification.evidence: signal-api container regained DNS and outbound; /v1/devices/+420720355763 went 400 'Closed unexpectedly' -> 200; the Signal bot answered !cat and !dog live at 18:28.

risks: Containers may now forward to the LAN, which is Docker's own default posture but is a relaxation of a bare default-drop forward chain
restore_docker_rules restarts dockerd, so containers without a restart policy stay down until started again
rollback: git revert the commit, then re-run setup_wireguard_ssh.sh (or nft -f /etc/nftables.conf) to reapply the previous ruleset
After rollback, expect bridged containers to lose outbound networking again: verify with 'docker run --rm --network bridge alpine wget -q -O /dev/null -T 6 https://1.1.1.1'
